title: Best Graphics Cards for Open-World Games in 2026, and a GTA 6 Reality Check
summary: GTA 6 has no PC version and won't stream to PC. Here are the eight graphics cards I'd buy for open-world games now, with 16GB VRAM front and centre.
body_markdown:
Let me deal with the GTA 6 question first, because it shapes everything else here. Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There is no announced PC version. And as of 7 October, there is no back door either: Xbox's chief strategy officer said the game will not stream to PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming, which put the earlier streaming reports to rest.


Rockstar's track record suggests a PC port will come eventually. GTA V reached PC about nineteen months after its console launch, and Red Dead Redemption 2 took about a year. But "eventually" is a poor reason to buy a graphics card today. A better reason is the open-world games you can play on PC right now, which lean on the same things: lots of video memory for textures, and steady frame pacing while you cross a big map.


## Why I Weight VRAM More Than Usual


In a corridor shooter, 12GB of VRAM goes a long way. In a dense open world at 1440p or 4K with high texture settings, I would rather have 16GB. It is the spec I check first before I look at clocks or cooler size. If I were buying a card I wanted to keep for three or four years, it would have 16GB.

## 4K Without Compromise: RTX 5080


The[GIGABYTE GeForce RTX 5080 Gaming OC](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932753?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) is the card I would buy for 4K. It has 16GB of GDDR7 on a 256-bit bus and a 360W rating, with a single 16-pin power connector. It is 340mm long, so measure the case before ordering.


## The Best Balance: RTX 5070 Ti vs RX 9070 XT


This is the matchup most people are deciding between. The[MSI GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Ventus 3X OC](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814137993?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) has 8,960 CUDA cores and 16GB of GDDR7 on a 256-bit bus, rated at 300W, and it is a fairly sensible 303mm long. The[ASRock Radeon RX 9070 XT Steel Legend](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814930136?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) brings 4,096 stream processors and 16GB of GDDR6, also on a 256-bit bus, at 304W, using two 8-pin connectors.


Both are excellent 1440p cards that can handle 4K with upscaling. My tie-breaker is software. If you lean on DLSS and NVIDIA's ray tracing features, take the 5070 Ti. If you would rather avoid a 16-pin connector, or you already run an AMD system and like the Adrenalin software, the 9070 XT is the one I would pick.


## The Quiet Middle: RX 9070


The[GIGABYTE Radeon RX 9070 Gaming OC](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932752?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) is the card I think gets overlooked. It keeps 16GB of GDDR6 on a 256-bit bus but is rated at 220W, with 3,584 stream processors. That lower power rating means less heat to deal with, and the listing's recommended power supply is 750W, a step down from the 800W suggested for the RX 9070 XT above.


## 12GB or 16GB in the Midrange


Here the head-to-head is about memory. The[MSI GeForce RTX 5070 Gaming Trio OC](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814137938?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) is the faster GPU, with 12GB of GDDR7 on a 192-bit bus, a 250W rating and MSI's 650W PSU recommendation. It is long for its class at 338mm. If you want something shorter and white, the[GIGABYTE RTX 5070 Eagle OC ICE](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932775?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) is the same GPU at 290mm.


The[MSI GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16G Gaming Trio OC](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814137954?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) has 16GB of GDDR7 but a narrower 128-bit bus and 4,608 CUDA cores, at 180W. On the AMD side, the[Sapphire Pulse Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814202457?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) is compact at 240mm, with 2,048 stream processors and a single 8-pin connector. For 1080p and lighter 1440p settings, I would take one of the 16GB cards over the 12GB 5070 if keeping the card a long time matters more than raw speed today.


## Winner by Category


4K: RTX 5080. Best all-round: RTX 5070 Ti, with the RX 9070 XT level with it if you prefer AMD. Efficient 16GB: RX 9070. Midrange speed: RTX 5070. Long-term budget pick: RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RX 9060 XT 16GB. Browse more in Newegg's[16GB graphics card listings](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=graphics+card+16gb&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-graphics-cards-open-world-2026) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is GTA 6 coming to PC?** Rockstar has not announced a PC version. The game launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on 19 November 2026.


**Can I stream GTA 6 to my PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming?** No. On 7 October 2026, Xbox's chief strategy officer said the game will not stream to PC through the cloud.


**How long did GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 take to reach PC?** GTA V arrived on PC in April 2015, about nineteen months after its September 2013 console launch. Red Dead Redemption 2 reached PC in November 2019, about a year after consoles.


**Is 12GB of VRAM enough for open-world games?** It works at 1080p and many 1440p settings, but high-resolution textures in big open worlds use a lot of memory. For a card you plan to keep for years, I would choose 16GB.


**Which power connector do these cards use?** The NVIDIA cards here use a single 16-pin connector. The RX 9070 XT and RX 9070 listed here use two 8-pin connectors, and the RX 9060 XT uses one 8-pin.
